questions.q: What can Lake Formation grant that a plain IAM policy on its own cannot?
options: The ability to encrypt data at rest
The ability to create new S3 buckets
Access to any AWS service at all — IAM cannot grant access to any service
Access scoped to a specific column, row, or cell within a table, not just the whole table or object
questions.explain: IAM's grain stops at the resource/API-call level. Lake Formation adds permissions at the table, column, row, and cell level on top of that.

questions.q: In Lake Formation's default 'Open' access-control method, what actually controls access to Data Catalog resources?
options: Lake Formation fine-grained permissions alone, with IAM playing no role
Nothing controls access by default — all data is public
IAM policies alone — Lake Formation's own fine-grained permissions are effectively bypassed via the Super permission on IAMAllowedPrincipals
A third-party identity provider, not AWS
questions.explain: The 'Open' method keeps backward compatibility with pre-Lake-Formation Glue setups by granting broad access via IAM, bypassing Lake Formation's finer controls.

questions.q: Which access-control method does AWS actually recommend?
options: Fine-grained IAM policies with no Lake Formation permissions at all
Disabling Lake Formation entirely and relying only on S3 bucket policies
The default 'Open' method, left unchanged
Fine-grained Lake Formation permissions with coarse-grained IAM policies
questions.explain: AWS's documentation recommends fine-grained Lake Formation permissions combined with coarser IAM policies — letting Lake Formation's own grants do the real restricting.

questions.q: What is the real advantage of granting access by LF-Tag instead of naming each table/column explicitly?
options: LF-Tags eliminate the need for any IAM permissions at all
LF-Tags are faster to query than named resources
A newly created, tagged resource is automatically covered by an existing tag-based grant — no new grant has to be written for it
LF-Tags can only be applied to entire databases, never individual columns
questions.explain: A grant written against a tag expression (e.g. department=sales) automatically applies to any resource carrying that tag, including ones created after the grant was written.

questions.q: Within a single LF-Tag key with multiple values, and across multiple different tag keys, how are the conditions combined in a tag expression?
options: Tag expressions can only ever use a single tag key
Everything is always AND'd together regardless of key
Everything is always OR'd together regardless of key
Values within one tag key are OR'd together; conditions across different tag keys are AND'd together
questions.explain: This combination (OR within a key, AND across keys) is what lets a tag expression express something like 'sales department AND not confidential' using two separate tag keys.
